findings.text: Huge-page clear operations at PMD and PUD granularity empty the slot and hand the prior entry back to the caller while informing the page-table checking layer with the address space, address and old value.
Native low-level clear helpers return the former PMD or PUD contents while zeroing the slot, using an atomic exchange on multiprocessor builds and a plain read plus clear on single-processor builds.

A PMD write-protect helper moves an entry toward read-only through a retrying atomic update so concurrent hardware dirty marking cannot create a forbidden encoding, and establish helpers publish a supplied PMD or PUD value while returning the displaced entry and notifying the checking layer.

Isolation translation derives kernel top-level pointers by clearing a reserved address bit and user pointers by setting the same bit, and a range clone helper duplicates PGD entries plus the shadow user copy only when the isolation mitigation is compiled and active on the processor.

Cache maintenance hooks for single PTE updates, fault ranges, and PMD and PUD updates are present but perform no action, indicating that no explicit synchronization is needed at those points on this architecture.

Swap entries support independent exclusivity, soft-dirty and userfaultfd annotations at PTE and where defined PMD granularity, each offering add, test and remove behavior that preserves the remaining entry bits.

Permission evaluation requires present and user status, additionally requires writable status for write requests, and finally consults the protection-key unit with the key decoded from entry flags; the same decision is exposed for PTE, PMD and PUD values, with key decoding yielding zero when protection keys are disabled.

Generic memory management invokes architecture hooks for cache refresh after table changes and for platform queries about failed pages, platform pages, zapped entries and pfn modification; here the cache hooks are no-ops and the platform and zapped-entry hooks are advertised as implemented.

User accessibility reports true only for present user mappings, with leaf status additionally required at PMD and PUD levels; hardware young tracking for non-leaf PMDs is unavailable under Xen paravirtualization, and pfn modification checking is needed only on processors affected by the L1TF flaw.

Kernel table utilities clear a 32-bit kernel PTE with a TLB flush, report five-level folding state, publish PTEs atomically, install P4D and PGD values while preserving the isolation shadow, reject kernel-half ranges for fast GUP, fold addresses through a virtual mask, and provide assembly helpers for page-aligned data and repeated PMD slots.

Multiprocessor builds make PMD and PUD publication and clearing atomic against concurrent walkers and updaters, while single-processor builds use ordered ordinary accesses because only local concurrency must be contained.

The isolation switch bit coincides with the page shift, clearing selects the kernel view and setting selects the user view in a reversible pair, and cloning copies the shadow only when the mitigation is both compiled and enabled, otherwise copying just the named range.
Write-clear dirty-set encodings are denied write access by the same present, user and writable tests that govern ordinary pages, and a protection-key denial overrides an otherwise permitted access.
Exclusivity, soft-dirty and userfaultfd marks live in distinct flag positions so manipulating one annotation does not disturb the others or the swap identity carried alongside them.

These helpers acquire no spinlock or sleepable lock; multiprocessor safety comes from single atomic exchanges or retrying compare exchanges, leaving higher-level table locking and TLB coordination to the caller.

Sixty-four-bit table values are unsigned long quantities wrapped in distinct single-field structures for each level and for protections, giving identical size and alignment with type separation between levels.

Thirty-two-bit fixed areas stack downward from the fixmap with the entry trampoline on top, then the LDT area, then the persistent kmap area, each aligned to a PMD boundary with a guard page, while vmalloc ends below the lower of the variable areas and modules alias the vmalloc extent.

A huge slot cycles between installed and empty through clear operations that return the evicted value and establish operations that install a new value while returning the displaced one, with the checking layer observing every transition in matching address-space context.

Permission checking advances from presence and user tests to write need and finally to protection-key allowance, failing closed at the first unsatisfied gate and succeeding only when each gate passes.

Non-atomic write clearing risks a race into a shadow-stack encoding, overwriting a differing present entry signals likely corruption, malformed entries are logged with location and raw value, and fast GUP must refuse addresses reaching the kernel half.

Isolation switching uses the page shift as bit position, PTE index width is the binary logarithm of entries per table, the swap-exclusive mark reuses the write-through position, and unmapped-area, top-down search and AGP page support are advertised.

Swap encoding reserves five high bits for type with the offset field starting just above the protection-none bit, provides complementary extract and construct conversions with offset complementing, and enforces at build time that the configured swapfile count fits the type width.

Sixty-four-bit geometry fixes 512 entries per table level with PMD shift twenty-one, PUD shift thirty and P4D shift thirty-nine, a variable PGD shift for four- and five-level modes, and size and mask pairs derived from each shift, with physical memory capped at fifty-two possible bits.

Sixty-four-bit reservations place maximum memory at one shifted by the physical-bit count, a sixteen-table guard hole starting at PGD entry minus 256, an LDT slot at minus 240, vmalloc bases ffffc90000000000 for four-level and ffa0000000000000 for five-level with spans 32 and 12800 terabytes, vmemmap bases ffffea0000000000 and ffd4000000000000, plus derived vmalloc start, size selector, memory end and quarter-size split.

Module space starts after the kernel image with ends ffffffffff000000 or fffffffffe000000 depending on configuration, fixup and entry trampolines sit at PGD entries minus two and minus four shifted by P4D width, the EFI window spans minus four to minus sixty-eight gigabytes, early tables number sixty-four, the kernel PGD start is half a page divided by entry size, KMSAN carves shadow and origin quarters from vmalloc plus module shadows, and the entry area holds a read-only IDT page followed by per-CPU pages.

Thirty-two-bit sizing sets an eight-megabyte vmalloc offset above high memory, kmap slots of 512 or 1024 entries across configs, entry-area pages as CPU count times the rounded entry structure size, table size as pages-per-PMD plus PGD count or pages-per-PGD, low pages as two gigabytes minus page offset shifted by page width, and PMD and PGD size-mask pairs from their shifts.

Feature and identity constants advertise arch-specific young, write-protect, huge-clear and invalidate support, alias the swapper directory to the initial top table, select the page-table sync scope by five-level state, expose same-entry comparison and vmemmap placement, extract the fourth-level index from bits thirty-nine to forty-seven, and guard headers against reinclusion.
